verses.1: When Rama, whose soul was known for righteousness, had been consecrated, the first night, which increased the joy of the citizens, passed.
verses.2: As that night dawned, in the morning, gentle bards, who were the awakeners of the king, stood near the king's palace.
verses.3: All of them, with melodious voices, trained like Kinnaras, greatly rejoicing, duly praised the heroic king.
verses.4: O heroic and gentle king, who increases Kausalya's joy, please awaken, for indeed, when you sleep, the entire world sleeps.
verses.5: Your valor is like that of Vishnu, your beauty is like that of the Ashvins, you are equal to Brihaspati in intellect, and indeed, you are like Prajapati himself.
verses.6: Your patience is like that of the earth, your splendor is comparable to the sun, your speed is equal to the wind, and your depth is like that of the ocean.
verses.7: You are unshakable like a pillar, and possess such gentleness as found in the moon; O king of men, there have been no such kings before, nor will there be in the future.
verses.8: As you are extremely formidable, always righteous, and devoted to the welfare of your subjects, O best among men, neither fame nor prosperity ever abandons you.
verses.9: O Rama, prosperity and righteousness are eternally established in you, and these and other sweet praises were sung by the bards.
verses.10: The bards, with their divine praises, awakened Rama, and Rama awoke to the sound of these eulogies being sung.
verses.11: He rose from that bed, which was covered with white sheets, just as Lord Narayana (Vishnu) rises from his serpent-bed.
verses.12: Thousands of humble men, with folded hands, approached the risen great-souled Rama, offering him water in pure vessels.
verses.13: Having purified himself with ablutions and offered oblations to the sacred fire at the appropriate time, he quickly went to the holy temple, which was traditionally frequented by the Ikshvaku kings.
verses.14: After duly worshipping the gods, ancestors, and Brahmins, Rama emerged into the outer chamber, surrounded by many people.
verses.15: All the great-souled ministers, along with their priests and headed by Vasishtha, approached Rama, shining brightly like fires.
verses.16: Great-souled Kshatriyas and rulers from various regions sat by Rama's side, just as the immortals sit by Indra.
verses.17: There, the highly renowned Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna attended upon Rama with delight, just as the three Vedas attend upon a sacrifice.
verses.18: Many servants with joyful faces came with folded hands and, indeed joyful, sat down by his side.
verses.19: Twenty greatly valorous and powerful monkeys, led by Sugriva, who can assume any form at will, serve Rama.
verses.20: And Vibhishana, surrounded by four rakshasas, serves the great-souled Rama, just as Guhyakas serve Kubera, the lord of wealth.
verses.21: Similarly, the wise elders of the guilds and noble-born men serve the king, Rama, having bowed down with their heads.
verses.22: Thus, the king Rama is surrounded by glorious sages, greatly valorous kings, monkeys, and rakshasas.
verses.23: Just as the lord of gods, Indra, is always served by sages, Rama shines with a splendor superior to that of the thousand-eyed Indra.
verses.24: To those who were seated, various very sweet stories imbued with righteousness were narrated by great souls who were learned in the Puranas. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 37 ।। Thus ends the thirty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
